answer: An agent network surveying willow wetlands along a coastal inlet treats unverified claims as a fable via random-walk filtering on a signed web-of-trust. Peers sign attestations only after verified exchanges, and routers score nodes using short random walks from trusted anchors. Because narrow attack cuts cap walk landings, each fake identity incurs scarce, verifiable service work with honest peers. However, compromised high-degree hubs can still admit large Sybil cliques.
